mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains depressed while TRANSIT stays below its recent average, weekday commuting demand will keep suppressing retail and recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the prior 28 days while WORKPLACES stays below -20 and TRANSIT stays below -10 on average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in GROCERY_PHARM indicates household errand consolidation and reduced out-of-home shopping, which should spill into retail and recreation weakness within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following 14 days after a week-on-week GROCERY_PHARM drop greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS surges while RESIDENTIAL also rises, discretionary outdoor substitution and at-home substitution jointly reduce shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC down over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall over the next 28 days in periods when PARKS is above 15 and RESIDENTIAL is above 2 simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in TRANSIT above baseline is a reopening signal that increases foot traffic near commercial areas, so retail and recreation should improve over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -10 and stays there for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following 28 days after TRANSIT remains above -10 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS remains elevated while GROCERY_PHARM falls back toward baseline, people are reallocating discretionary time toward leisure outside the retail corridor, which should leave retail and recreation weaker over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is above 20 and GROCERY_PHARM is below 2 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move lower in the week after PARKS exceeds 20 while GROCERY_PHARM is below 2.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PARKS with stable WORKPLACES indicates a leisure-heavy seasonal pattern that diverts spending from indoor retail, producing a lower RETAIL_REC mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days when PARKS averages above 15 and WORKPLACES remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep falling, then a policy tightening or mobility shock is constraining trip generation, which should suppress retail and recreation within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops below -28 while TRANSIT drops below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 14 days after WORKPLACES falls below -28 and TRANSIT falls below -15 together.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rebound in GROCERY_PHARM while RESIDENTIAL eases back from elevated levels signals more errands outside the home, which should lift retail and recreation over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM trends upward and RESIDENTIAL stays flat or declines.
